description:
Advances: ancora.findings, ancora.scaffold

Findings: F7 (High, api H3 + spec L3). Individual report: 20260904-061300-api.md beside ~/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-04/ancora-xla-post-ship-hardening/20260904-061300-consolidated.md.

Deliverable:
README.md:53-59 and docs/migration.md:32-41 tell users to promote a Spec-Ack trailer into config using an optional `requirement:` key in an overrides entry, naming Argos, Engage, Builder and Atlas as the audience. Ancora.Config has no such key: parse_override_entry (config.ex:392) reads only subject, code, severity and reason and drops anything else with no diagnostic, so the override silently applies subject-wide instead of requirement-scoped and the gate suppresses more than the author asked for. The key belongs to ancora-gg8.1 on the other epic branch and is not in this tree.
Fix: reword README.md and docs/migration.md to say overrides are scoped to a subject and a code in this release (and, if you keep a forward reference, say plainly that the key is not accepted yet and what happens if written); make Config reject unsupported keys inside an overrides entry with a config finding (config/invalid_value or config/unknown_key; state which in the spec) so a written `requirement:` key is a loud error, not a silent widening; drop the forward-reference paragraph from .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.durable_acknowledgments.md; check priv/spec_init/agents/SKILL.md and priv/spec_init/README.md for the same instruction and fix them if present.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/config_test.exs, test/ancora/scaffold/docs_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate:
  1. A .spec/config.yml with an overrides entry carrying `requirement:` (or any unknown key) makes `mix spec.check` report a config finding naming the key and the entry, and the override is NOT applied. Mutation: restore the silent drop; the test must fail.
  2. A well-formed overrides entry still applies exactly as before (regression).
  3. README.md and docs/migration.md no longer instruct writing a `requirement:` key (docs test asserts the promotion paragraph's content by normalized text, not a fragile substring). Mutation: reintroduce the sentence; the test must fail.
- Spec edit required in-diff: ancora.findings (config family) shall state that unknown keys inside an overrides entry are a config finding and the entry is not applied; ancora.scaffold only if the scaffold docs change. Decision-record edit: ancora.decision.durable_acknowledgments loses the forward reference and records the 1.x scope of overrides.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: compile-graph-scoped checks only (`mix test --stale` or the named files) plus `mix spec.validate`; run `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` as a dev-loop check as soon as the spec edit exists, before either capped final-tier run.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, the named test files, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix deps.unlock --check-unused`, `mix spec.check --base e18fa05`, run-until-green. Full suite runs at the orchestrator's merge gate.
  - Verifier tier: `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` plus targeted selections; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test that fails under the named mutation; prove each ordered test both ways and report the numbers
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh: the substantive requirement or scenario edit named below lands in the same diff with its decision-record edit; never a Spec-Ack trailer; never weaken a must
  - Fixtures never call production functions (use test/support or System.cmd); under file-scoped derivation a stray call binds a subject
  - Grader scratch discipline applies to you too: work only in this worktree, address it by absolute path
- Call-site Integration: Config.load/1 is called once from Preflight; prove through the CLI fixture, not the config unit test alone.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/trailer.ex, lib/ancora/gate.ex, lib/ancora/severity.ex, lib/ancora/review/**, lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex, lib/ancora/git/**, lib/ancora/derive/**, lib/mix/tasks/**
Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/config.ex
- README.md, docs/migration.md, priv/spec_init/agents/SKILL.md, priv/spec_init/README.md, priv/spec_init/config.yml.eex (documentation of overrides only)
- test/ancora/**, test/mix/tasks/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.findings.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.scaffold.spec.md (substantive edits named above; never weakening a must)
- .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.durable_acknowledgments.md
- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (binding-aware clause: derivation is file-scoped, so acknowledgment edits only, one substantive sentence describing what this ticket changed as that subject observes it, verified by execution; if the subject observes nothing, say so in the completion record and stop)
- .spec/decisions/** (every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; write a real contract statement, never a hollow line)

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do not implement requirement-scoped overrides (ancora-gg8.1 owns that on its branch). Do not change the severities map handling. Do not rebase; base stays e18fa05.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes (`mix spec.check --base e18fa05` result=pass)
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

Summary: Config now rejects unknown override-entry keys with non-tunable config/unknown_key findings, ignores those entries, and the real CLI fixture proves the rejected override cannot suppress its subject finding. README and migration promotion guidance now documents the subject-and-code scope accepted by Ancora 1.x, pinned by normalized paragraph assertions and matching spec and decision edits. Mutation proofs were behavior 1 at 22 tests, 1 failure mutated and 22 tests, 0 failures restored; behavior 2 at 15 tests, 1 failure mutated and 15 tests, 0 failures restored; behavior 3 at 3 tests, 1 failure mutated and 3 tests, 0 failures restored.

TEST_CRITIC: PASS

Reviewed aa5e8c1 over e18fa05. Three added tests, all additive; no existing
assertion in config_test.exs, docs_test.exs or spec_check_test.exs was
loosened or deleted. Ran test/ancora/config_test.exs and
test/ancora/scaffold/docs_test.exs (18 tests, 0 failures) and
test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:382 (1 test, 0 failures) from the stage
worktree.

PER-ASSERTION VERDICT

1. CLI test proves NOT-applied. PASS.
   test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:382 does not stop at "a config finding
   appeared". It asserts the suppressed subject finding still fires with its
   default severity: code derived/unanchored_subject, subject sample.subject,
   severity "warning". Had the entry been applied it would render "info" and
   drop out of the gated set. Backed by exit status 1 and the fail verdict
   last on stdout.
   Reachability is established, not assumed: `assert Enum.any?(...)` cannot
   pass vacuously, and the file passes, so both findings are genuinely present
   in the parsed JSON report.
   The one thing reading alone cannot settle is whether "warning" is a live
   discriminator or a value that would appear even if overrides never applied
   through the subprocess path at all. That is answered by the positive
   control at test/ancora/gate_test.exs:751, where a well-formed override on
   the same code downgrades sample.a to :info and drops it from
   report.findings while sample.b stays :warning. Same Gate.check path
   spec.check drives. I consider the discriminator sound.
   MUTATION FOR THE VERIFIER IF YOU WANT IT AIRTIGHT IN THIS FILE: drop the
   `unknown_keys` clause from parse_override/3 in lib/ancora/config.ex so the
   entry is accepted. The second Enum.any? at line 405 must fail (severity
   flips to "info").

2. Config unit test names the key and the entry. PASS WITH A GAP.
   test/ancora/config_test.exs:164 asserts `config.overrides == []` by
   equality, which is the strongest available not-applied proof at this
   layer. It names the key as `~s("requirement")` (quoted form, so it matches
   the inspected key, not an incidental prose occurrence) and names the entry
   via the "atlas.web.sessions" substring inside the inspected map.
   On "entry index": the repo spec scenario
   ancora.findings.scenario.override_unknown_key requires the finding to name
   "requirement and the entry", not an index, and the implementation names
   the whole inspected entry. No index exists to assert. I judged against the
   spec.
   GAP (warning, not blocking): both the unit test and the CLI test match the
   entry only by its subject id. A mutation that shortened the finding key to
   name just the subject and dropped the inspected entry would survive both,
   while violating "naming ... the entry". Tightening: assert
   `finding.key =~ "in overrides entry"` or match the code and severity
   fields too.

3. Docs test normalization and paragraph content. PASS.
   test/ancora/scaffold/docs_test.exs:27 collapses all whitespace through
   String.split |> Enum.join(" ") and asserts full-paragraph EQUALITY against
   both README.md and docs/migration.md. Not a fragile substring, and not a
   needle either: re-adding any `requirement:` instruction inside that
   paragraph changes the string and fails.
   DELETION DOES NOT PASS. promotion_paragraphs/1 uses Enum.find, which
   returns nil when the paragraph is gone; normalize(nil) calls
   String.split(nil), which raises ArgumentError (verified by running it).
   The test errors rather than silently passing. It fails loudly, though as
   an ArgumentError rather than a readable assertion diff.
   GAP (recommendation): the guard is scoped to that one paragraph in each
   file. A `requirement:` instruction re-added as a NEW paragraph elsewhere
   in README.md or docs/migration.md would pass. Neither file carries a
   blanket refute on the key. Both files currently mention "requirement" only
   in unrelated senses (requirement ids, the code map rows), so a blanket
   refute would need to target `requirement:` in an overrides context.

4. Well-formed entry still applies. PASS, and it was already there.
   test/ancora/config_test.exs:243 "an override applies only to the named
   subject" is untouched and asserts subject.a resolves to :info with
   severity_source :config, subject.b stays :warning/:default, and
   subject_status returns :acknowledged for a only. The end-to-end twin at
   gate_test.exs:751 is also untouched. The new unknown-key tests sit beside
   these rather than replacing them.

5. Source-text pinning of lib/ancora/config.ex. NONE ADDED.
   All three new tests assert on behavior (loaded config, resolved severity,
   JSON report, file content of docs). The pre-existing moduledoc needle test
   in the "co-versioning note" describe block is unchanged, and the
   moduledoc edit in this commit left its three needles (mix.lock, same PR,
   dependency) intact.

6. Weakening check. NONE.
   git diff e18fa05..HEAD -- test/ is purely additive: 24 lines in
   config_test.exs, 27 in docs_test.exs, 34 in spec_check_test.exs. No
   deletions, no relaxed matchers, no removed tags.

UNVERIFIED BY READING
None that block. The single reachability question (item 1) was resolved by
running the file, since the assertion form cannot pass vacuously. The named
mutation is offered as belt-and-braces for the verifier, not as an
outstanding doubt.
